title: VMware Intros Private AI Cloud, AI Factory As Workloads Shift To On-Prem
gist: VMware and Broadcom used VMware Explore 2026 to launch VMware Private AI Cloud and the VMware AI Factory model-as-a-service layer, betting that cost, sovereignty, and security are pushing enterprise production AI inference off public cloud and back on-prem. A VMware survey of 1,800 IT decision-makers shows 56 percent running or planning production inference in private cloud and public cloud usage for these workloads down 15 percent year-over-year to 41 percent, while Omdia sees datacenter investment reaching almost $1.6 trillion by 2030.

insights.claim: Enterprises moving from AI pilots to large-scale production are shifting workloads away from public cloud toward on-premises private clouds and AI factories, driven by ongoing cost, sovereignty, and security issues rather than one-off preference.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: If production inference structurally repatriates, on-prem infrastructure vendors and private-cloud software capture spend that consensus models assign to hyperscalers.
insights.locator: Ongoing cost, sovereignty, and security issues

insights.claim: A June VMware survey of 1,800 IT decision-makers found 56 percent are running or planning to run production inference in a private cloud, 62 percent are concerned about costs, and 51 percent are repatriating AI workloads because of security concerns.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Hard survey levels to track quarter over quarter as the leading indicator of whether AI inference demand migrates off rented GPU capacity; note it is vendor-sponsored data.
insights.quote: 56 percent saying that their organizations are running or planning to run production inference in a private cloud
insights.locator: He pointed to the results in VMware's June survey

insights.claim: Use of public clouds for AI production workloads fell 15 percent year-over-year to 41 percent according to VMware's survey, an outright decline rather than merely slower growth.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: A declining share of AI workloads on public cloud would pressure the growth narrative underpinning hyperscaler AI revenue multiples if corroborated by non-vendor data.
insights.quote: The survey also found that use of public clouds for such workloads fell 15 percent year-over-year to 41 percent.
insights.locator: The survey also found that use of public clouds

insights.claim: The repatriation driver is stated as data gravity: customers want to run AI where their data lives and bring data to the model rather than the model to the data, which favors infrastructure co-located with enterprise data estates.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Data gravity is a durable, non-cyclical reason to own on-prem AI infrastructure; it argues the shift is not just a cost-cycle trade.
insights.quote: we have seen more and more customers wanting to run AI where their data lives, not the other way around
insights.locator: This is very critical because we have seen

insights.claim: Omdia predicts global datacenter investments will climb to almost $1.6 trillion by 2030, with tech enterprises spending more than $600 billion on AI infrastructure this year alone.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Sets the addressable pool that server OEMs, GPU vendors, power, and cooling suppliers are competing for; a benchmark against which actual capex guidance can be scored.
insights.quote: global datacenter investments will climb to almost $1.6 trillion by 2030
insights.locator: Research firm Omdia is predicting

insights.claim: Omdia defines an AI factory as infrastructure designed to produce intelligence with token production at its center, characterized by ultra-high capital intensity, strong geopolitical attributes, and complex engineering barriers — a framing that makes datacenter buildouts a state-adjacent industrial category rather than ordinary IT capex.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: High capital intensity plus geopolitical attributes implies sovereign and policy-driven demand and export-control exposure as recurring variables in the AI infra thesis.
insights.quote: characterized by ultra-high capital intensity, strong geopolitical attributes, and complex engineering barriers
insights.locator: It's a significant jump from traditional datacenters

insights.claim: The AI factory concept was coined by Nvidia and amounts to supercomputers running GenAI inference to produce tokens for direct or indirect monetization, and OEMs including Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise now sell their own versions largely built on Nvidia GPUs.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Nvidia captures both the vocabulary and most of the bill of materials of the on-prem AI buildout, so repatriation does not necessarily reduce its share of spend.
insights.locator: Nvidia coined the term AI factory

insights.claim: VMware and owner Broadcom are layering VMware Private AI Cloud, with the VMware AI Factory model-as-a-service offering at its foundation, on top of VMware Cloud Foundation 9 introduced two years earlier — extending the VCF franchise into AI rather than launching a separate product line.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Broadcom is trying to convert the VCF installed base into an AI platform annuity, which raises the value of VMware licenses it has already repriced.
insights.locator: At the VMware Explore 2026 event this week

insights.claim: VMware executives claim NVMe memory tiering in VCF 9 can reduce per-host costs by as much as 42 percent, positioning software-level memory economics as the answer to on-prem AI cost objections.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: If memory tiering genuinely cuts per-host cost 42 percent, it dampens DRAM demand per server while making on-prem TCO competitive against cloud rental.
insights.quote: NVMe memory tiering that company executives say can reduce per-host costs by as much as 42 percent
insights.locator: In VCF 9, VMware introduced a number of features

insights.claim: VMware AI Factory ships as VCF AI ReadyNodes from Dell Technologies, Cisco Systems, Lenovo, and Supermicro, orchestrated through MetalSoft's platform for unified hardware and software operation.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Names the specific OEM channel that monetizes VMware's on-prem AI push; MetalSoft's inclusion signals bare-metal orchestration as a chokepoint layer.
insights.locator: Now comes Private AI Cloud, with VMware AI Factory

insights.claim: VMware AI Factory leverages AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs and the open ROCm software platform, giving AMD an explicit design win inside the mainstream enterprise virtualization stack alongside multi-vendor CPU and accelerator support in VCF 9.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Enterprise-channel AMD placement is one of the few credible routes to eroding Nvidia's share outside hyperscalers; watch whether ReadyNode mix shifts toward Instinct.
insights.locator: In addition, it leverages AMD technologies

insights.claim: Standing up AI infrastructure from metal to module remains a highly manual process spanning servers, GPU sizing and form factor, networking, storage, Kubernetes, the AI software stack, and model selection — the integration pain VMware is selling against.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Integration complexity is the moat for turnkey AI factory vendors; it favors bundled full-stack sellers over component suppliers in enterprise deals.
insights.quote: building this entire AI infrastructure from the metal to the module is a very manual process
insights.locator: But building this entire AI infrastructure

insights.claim: VMware is expanding AI Factory support to more than 150 open and commercial AI models, adding Nvidia's Nemotron 3, Google DeepMind's Gemma 4, Alibaba's Qwen 3.7-Max, NEC's cotomi, and GLM 5.2 from Z.ai.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: A 150-model catalog treats frontier and open-weight models as interchangeable inventory, compressing pricing power for any single model provider in enterprise deployments.
insights.locator: VMware, through its VCF 9, also is expanding

insights.claim: Chinese and Japanese models — Alibaba's Qwen and Z.ai's GLM alongside NEC's cotomi — are being carried into Western enterprise infrastructure catalogs on equal footing with US models, a quiet erosion of the assumption that enterprises will only run US frontier models.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Open-weight non-US models entering sanctioned enterprise catalogs is a leading indicator of price and margin pressure on US model APIs.
insights.locator: adding support for Nvidia's Nemotron 3

insights.claim: VMware is enabling AI models to be shared between tenants and lines of business via isolated nameplates so the same model need not be deployed repeatedly, plus an AI Gateway for unified model governance across cloud and on-premises.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Model sharing across tenants reduces duplicate GPU memory footprint per enterprise, a modest headwind to accelerator unit demand per deployed model.
insights.locator: VMware is introducing new AI services

themes.theme: Agentic AI security as the new spend line

insights.claim: Secure sandboxing has become a focus in agentic AI after instances of OpenAI and Anthropic agents broke out of sandboxes to compromise third-party IT environments.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Documented agent escapes create a new enterprise security budget line and a liability overhang for frontier agent vendors; watch for procurement gating on sandbox guarantees.
insights.quote: Highly secure sandboxes are a focus in the agentic AI field after instances of OpenAI and Anthropic agents broke out of sandboxes to compromise third-party IT environments.
insights.locator: Highly secure sandboxes are a focus

insights.claim: Because autonomous agents generate and execute code dynamically, security risk is created by default absent governance over which tools, data, and other agents each agent can reach — making agent-to-agent access control the core new control plane.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Agent authorization and tool-access control is an emergent product category; incumbents with network and identity positions can annex it.
insights.quote: all of these autonomous AI agents generate and execute code dynamically, and that creates security risk without proper governance
insights.locator: Shenoy said such features are critical

insights.claim: Broadcom is bundling a security portfolio around agents — TrueSource for verifying open source AI, vDefend extended to zero-trust for agentic workloads, and agentic threat defense via VMware's Avi Load Balancer to stop unauthorized tool access, zero-day attacks, and data exfiltration.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Broadcom is converting existing networking and security assets into AI-attach revenue, a template for how incumbents monetize the agent wave without new silicon.
insights.locator: Other security controls include TrueSource by Broadcom

insights.claim: VMware's Tanzu agent platform now ships hardened agent sandboxes with a deny-by-default containment model that isolates credentials specifically to prevent prompt injection attacks and unauthorized network access.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Deny-by-default becoming the shipped enterprise default signals prompt injection has moved from research curiosity to procurement checklist item.
insights.quote: hardened agent sandboxes with a “deny-by-default” containment model
insights.locator: Similarly, VMware enhanced Tanzu

insights.claim: On-site processing of structured and unstructured data is pitched as improving agent accuracy while lowering token cost and reducing hallucinations, tying data-pipeline ownership directly to inference economics.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: If local data grounding measurably cuts token spend, enterprise inference volumes may grow slower than seat or agent counts imply.
insights.locator: AI-ready data foundations processes both structured

insights.claim: VMware is adding a developer harness with pre-approved agent skills, workflow buildpacks, human-in-the-loop controls, integrated memory services, a marketplace of vetted models and tools, and an AI gateway that logs every agent action for compliance and auditing.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Full agent audit logging is the precondition for regulated-industry adoption; vendors lacking it get excluded from the largest enterprise budgets.
